title: Saturday 4 April 2026
headline: Key Developments in Financial Auditing and Disclosure Standards
intro: On 4 April 2026, significant updates emerged regarding the auditing of financial statements and the evolving landscape of financial disclosures in Europe. The European Supervisory Authorities (ESAs) have reported increased efforts from market participants in disclosing principal adverse impacts, reflecting a growing commitment to transparency. Additionally…
summary: The statutory audit remains a cornerstone of financial accountability, ensuring that companies and public entities provide accurate financial statements. By certifying these records, audits offer stakeholders, including investors and shareholders, a reliable opinion on the financial health of entities. This process not only enhances trust but also underpins the integrity of financial markets across Europe. In tandem with auditing practices, the ESAs have observed a notable increase in the efforts of financial market participants to disclose principal adverse impacts. This trend is documented in the latest report from the Joint Committee of the ESAs, which underscores the importance of transparency in sustainable finance. Enhanced disclosures are vital for assessing the broader implications of financial activities on environmental and social factors, aligning with regulatory expectations…
key_points: The ESAs note greater effort from financial market participants in their disclosure of principal adverse impacts
